title: Three-Dimensional Chess Anyone? The Challenges of Power Integrity for Multi-Die Designs
gist: Summarizing a Synopsys white paper, the piece argues that multi-die 2.5D/3D designs make power integrity a full-stack system property, with five recurring failure modes, and that EMIR/thermal analysis must move early and run concurrently across the stack using tools like 3DIC Compiler and RedHawk-SC.

insights.claim: In multi-die 2.5D/3D designs, power travels through package connections, interposers, TSVs, TIVs, micro-bumps and hybrid bonds, so power integrity becomes a property of the entire interconnected stack rather than an individual die.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Raises EDA content per design for multi-die and favors vendors with full-stack analysis.
insights.quote: power integrity is no longer a property of an individual die. It is a property of the entire interconnected system.
insights.locator: The Power Delivery Network Has Changed

insights.claim: Power delivery networks in advanced AI accelerators may carry kilowatt-class power, so even small resistance increases cause significant voltage drops.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Power delivery is a gating constraint on AI accelerator scaling.

insights.claim: A switching event on one die can disturb voltage on neighboring dies through shared power-delivery resources, so analyzing dies independently misses stack-level interactions.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Per-die signoff flows are inadequate; demand for stack-aware tools rises.
insights.locator: A switching event on one die

insights.claim: Synopsys identifies five recurring multi-die power delivery failure modes: missing vias/excess resistance, insufficient TSVs, inadequate micro-bump connectivity, redistribution-layer electromigration, and thermal interactions.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Checklist for diligence on 3D-IC design risk.

insights.claim: Heat from neighboring dies and interconnects raises resistance and accelerates electromigration, so multi-die failure modes compound: a weak interface can simultaneously worsen IR drop, current crowding and thermal reliability.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Thermal and electrical co-analysis is required, boosting electrothermal tool demand.

themes.theme: Why legacy EMIR tools fall short

insights.claim: Advanced interposers use irregular non-Manhattan geometries that traditional extraction can model inaccurately, requiring adaptive-mesh extraction to avoid misleading IR-drop or electromigration results.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Tool accuracy differentiation matters in 3D-IC EDA.

insights.claim: Modern multi-die assemblies may contain tens of millions of micro-bumps and hybrid bonds, creating electrical networks far larger than single-die EMIR tools were designed to handle.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Compute-scalable EDA (and compute farms) become necessary for signoff.

insights.claim: Teams trade accuracy for capacity by analyzing representative vertical slices of repetitive 3D structures, using large compute farms for full detail, or employing reduced-order models.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Methodology choice affects design schedules and compute spend.

insights.claim: Synopsys recommends moving EMIR analysis earlier through a five-stage methodology: architectural exploration, interposer analysis, early prototyping, concurrent static analysis, and concurrent dynamic analysis.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Shift-left expands EDA usage earlier in the design cycle.
insights.locator: Find Power Integrity Problems Before Signoff

insights.claim: Discovering insufficient TSVs, weak power grids or excess resistance near tapeout can force redesign of power networks and routing, disrupting timing closure.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Late power-integrity discoveries are a schedule-risk driver for multi-die chips.

insights.claim: Accurate EMIR analysis can reduce over-design by avoiding unnecessary power-grid margins that cost area, power and money, and AI-driven analysis helps find hotspots and root causes as schedules compress.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Better analysis has direct silicon cost payback, supporting EDA pricing.

insights.claim: Synopsys's multi-die power integrity flow combines 3DIC Compiler with RedHawk-SC, Totem-SC and RedHawk-SC Electrothermal for concurrent analysis across digital, custom, memory, interposer and package structures.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: RedHawk/Totem (ex-Ansys) integration into Synopsys flows strengthens its multi-die franchise.
insights.locator: Integrating Power Integrity into the Design Flow
